name: Our Lady of Guadalupe
history: In December 1531 the Virgin appeared to Juan Diego, a poor Aztec convert, on the hill of Tepeyac. As a sign for the bishop she filled his cloak with Castilian roses, and when he opened it her image was found printed on it. Millions were baptised in the years that followed.
meditation: Am I not here, I who am your mother? Bring her your greatest worry.
life: Juan Diego was a Nahua man, born around 1474, who had been baptised by Franciscan missionaries a few years after the Spanish conquest of Mexico. On 9 December 1531, walking to Mass, he heard music on the hill of Tepeyac and saw a young woman who spoke to him in his own language and asked for a church to be built there. Bishop Juan de Zumárraga asked for a sign. On 12 December, hurrying to find a priest for his dying uncle, Juan Diego tried to avoid the hill, but the Lady met him, promised his uncle's healing and sent him to gather roses on its frozen summit. When he opened his cloak before the bishop, the roses fell and the image was there. The account was written down in Nahuatl, and the Church has approved the apparitions as private revelation. Juan Diego was canonised in 2002.
prayerTo: Our Lady of Guadalupe, you came to a poor man and spoke to him tenderly in his own tongue. You are here, our mother. Take under your mantle the peoples of the Americas, the poor and the forgotten, mothers and their unborn children, and me in my troubles. Bring us all to your Son. Amen.
penance: Bring flowers to an image of Our Lady today, and give to a charity that supports mothers and babies in need.
